answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with voucher-capped onboarding. Each established agent may sponsor only a few newcomers and must lock a bond that is slashed if those invitees later behave as a coordinated nebula of clones. New identities begin at a reputation nadir of zero voting weight until the lock matures, so disposable accounts cannot influence outcomes immediately. The attacker then faces a cost spiral: bonded capital and waiting time grow with every extra identity, while honest agents pay that cost only once.
